title: Fruits lowest in calories

seo.title: Fruits lowest in calories
seo.meta_description: Among common fresh fruits, lemon has ~29 calories/100 g; watermelon and lime 30; strawberries 32; cantaloupe 34; peach 39; grapefruit 42 and blackberries 43. High water content drives the ranking.
seo.search_intent: Rank common fresh fruits with the lowest calories per 100 g and explain how water content, serving size and overall nutrition affect the practical meaning.

excerpt: The lowest-calorie fresh fruits are generally those with the most water and very little fat. Reference values per 100 g include lemon ~29 calories, watermelon and lime 30, strawberries 32, cantaloupe 34, peach 39, pink/red grapefruit 42 and blackberries 43. Per-100-g figures compare energy density; realistic serving sizes still change how many calories you eat.
content_html:
For fresh fruit, very low calories usually come from a simple formula: a lot of water and very little fat. Watermelon, strawberries and melon can therefore fill considerable space on a plate without concentrating much energy.

Ranking per 100 grams

These USDA reference values use raw edible fruit so the energy density is compared on the same basis.

FruitCalories per 100 g
Lemon29 kcal
Watermelon30 kcal
Lime30 kcal
Strawberries32 kcal
Cantaloupe34 kcal
Peach39 kcal
Pink/red grapefruit42 kcal
Blackberries43 kcal

Watermelon at 30 calories and blackberries at 43 differ by only 13 calories per 100 g. That is too small a gap to turn the table into a health score; fiber, micronutrients and serving size can matter more.

Water content drives much of the ranking

Watermelon is roughly 91% water, and cantaloupe is around 90%. That leaves relatively little dry matter per 100 g to contribute energy.

Strawberries follow the same pattern: mostly water, with very little fat.

Lemon and lime rank low but have unusual servings

Their per-100-g calorie values are low, but few people eat 7 ounces of lemon as dessert. Their ranking position describes concentration, not a typical serving recommendation.

Watermelon is the opposite: a 200–300 g portion is easy to eat, so total calories rise even though its energy density stays low.

Real portions put the numbers in context

150 g strawberries provide about 48 calories, while 250 g watermelon provides around 75 calories. About 150 g edible peach is roughly 59 calories.

All are modest amounts in the context of a meal, and choosing among them to save ten calories is usually less useful than choosing whole fruit you actually enjoy.

Lower calorie does not mean nutritionally superior

Avocado has about 160 calories per 100 g because it contains much more fat, but it also provides fiber, potassium and predominantly unsaturated fat. Raspberries have 52 calories per 100 g—higher than strawberries—while supplying around 6.5 g fiber.

Energy density answers one question; it is not an overall nutrition score.

faq.question: What fruit has the fewest calories?
faq.answer: Among common references, lemon is about 29 calories per 100 g and watermelon and lime about 30. Lemon and lime are normally eaten in much smaller portions, however.

faq.question: How many calories are in 100 g of strawberries?
Is the lowest-calorie fruit always the healthiest?
faq.answer: No. Calories measure energy; fiber, fats, vitamins, minerals and serving size also matter.
